bibliographic.title: A comprehensive review of large language models: issues and solutions in learning environments
bibliographic.authors: Tariq Shahzad; Tehseen Mazhar; Muhammad Usman Tariq; Wasim Ahmad; Khmaies Ouahada; Habib Hamam
bibliographic.citation_apa: Shahzad, T., Mazhar, T., Tariq, M. U., Ahmad, W., Ouahada, K., & Hamam, H. (2025). A comprehensive review of large language models: Issues and solutions in learning environments. Discover Sustainability, 6, 27. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43621-025-00815-8

methodology.study_design: comprehensive review with proposed theoretical framework
methodology.technology_context: large language models (including ChatGPT-4) applied in digital and higher education learning environments

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed comprehensive review focused on LLMs in education, proposing a theoretical integration framework and addressing ethical barriers such as data privacy and bias. Provided text supports relevance to regulated learning contexts and generic governance concerns, but does not substantiate a primary focus on conversational governance, conversational systems, observability, audit, or compliance mechanisms required for central evidence in this review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter (pages 1-2) was supplied; full review methods, case studies, and governance solutions cannot be verified.

appraisal.notes: Abstract and introduction clearly state aims and education focus, but supplied text does not describe review search strategy, inclusion criteria, corpus size, or analytical procedure beyond claiming a systematic analysis.

cerqual.explanation: Coherent framing of LLM issues in education and ethical challenges is present, but methodological detail and governance-specific findings are insufficient in the provided excerpts to support high-confidence synthesis.

coding.theme: LLM adoption and ethical integration in learning environments
coding.subtheme: barriers and solutions for privacy, bias, and pedagogical concerns
rq_alignment: LLM governance themes in regulated education
ethical and risk barriers to LLM deployment

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs can transform education, but their integration requires a structured framework that addresses personalization, ethical concerns, adaptability, data privacy, and bias.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a comprehensive review of LLMs in learning environments and proposes a novel theoretical framework with practical case studies and solutions to educational barriers.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text does not document review methodology, sample of studies, or detailed governance mechanisms; conversational-AI-specific governance is not evidenced.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on ethical and practical barriers to LLM use in regulated education settings; not sufficient as central evidence for conversational governance architecture or operational controls.
